articles.title: Bruno Fernandes reveals talks over new Manchester United contract are on hold
articles.summary: Club captain confirms he has been offered a new deal. ‘Not the right moment to be talking about negotiations’ Bruno Fernandes has revealed that Manchester United have offered him a new contract, but discussions have been ⁠put on hold as the club focuses on turning around its terrible start to the…
body: Fernandes’ current deal expires at the end of this campaign, although United ⁠hold an ​option to extend their captain’s contract by a further year until June 2028, giving the club more time to reach ⁠an agreement on fresh terms.

“The club offered me a new contract so I think that, from their side, shows that they ⁠want me to stay. And as you said, there are no negotiations going on,” ​ Fernandes told Sky Sports in an ‌interview published on Sunday.

The 32-year-old’s future is still up in the air after it was revealed he turned down a second contract offer from the club. Fernandes’ form has dropped off this season, his goal and assist in the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa providing his first goal involvements in the league since scoring a hat-trick against Ipswich in August.
The Portugal international also hit back at rumours he had demanded more money and a longer deal, ​saying his priority was to remain at Old Trafford and help restore the club’s fortunes.

articles.title: Robins ‘aims for the stars’ as Stoke dream of Premier League return
articles.summary: The Championship’s form side climbed to second after holding on resiliently with 10 men to knock Birmingham off the summit. There have been false dawns before. Plenty of them.
body: Experience has taught the benefit of pragmatism, so no one will be getting ahead of themselves just yet. But this weekend was supposed to be the big test for Mark Robins’s team and few considered they would pass it quite so resoundingly.

Facing a Birmingham side who arrived top of the table and with firmly held Premier League ambitions, Stoke dominated for an hour, the hitherto goal-shy George Hirst earning a well-deserved lead to send a bumper crowd into raptures. The hand-wringing that then followed Luca Bombino’s sending-off with half an hour remaining made the victory that followed all the sweeter. The 10 men of Stoke were superb. It was no surprise that it took considerable time to convince those in the stands to depart for home after the final whistle.

You see, it is not just that Stoke are second in the table, kept off top spot by goal difference. It is not even that they are undoubtedly the Championship’s form side, with just one defeat in their past 13 games. It is the whole feeling around the place; the resilience Robins has developed, and the belief that they can take on the big guns and beat them.

articles.title: César Azpilicueta: ‘At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe – if you can’t perform, you’re out’
articles.summary: Former defender reflects on his record-breaking longevity, kicking Eden Hazard in training, and life after retirement. César Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the…
body: It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. And although he hasn’t found a seven-a-side team yet he will.

“I get up, take them to school, go to the gym. I do pilates some days. I walk the dogs, play golf, then it’s after-school activities. I read, try to learn new things. I haven’t yet thought: ‘I’m bored,’” Azpilicueta says, although you wonder how long that will last. “Over the last 12 months I could see it. The summer before I already ‘hit the post’ with retirement. It’s natural: a day comes … if only I could play for ever but it is what it is and you have to keep evolving. I’m enjoying it.”

articles.title: 'Let fantastically promising McConnell loose against Pumas'
articles.summary: Scotland head into their Nations Championship finale against Argentina on a high and should unleash Liam McConnell on the Pumas after his hat-trick against Japan, writes Tom English.
body: Having lost at home to Argentina in November and then beating Argentina away from home in July, Scotland's next joust with the Pumas is set for Twickenham next Sunday, 29 November - fourth from the northern hemisphere versus fourth from the south on the final day of the Nations Championship.
The warm-up act before the grand final between France and South Africa later on Sunday is not where Scotland wanted to be, but four wins from six games is a decent return.
A fifth win in seven would be encouraging, if not life-changing for this team. They've all been at this rodeo before.
On Saturday, Scotland's much-changed team tore an understrength, over-powered and severely out-matched Japan to shreds. Eleven tries was bordering on an exhibition.

articles.title: NFL player Harrell in hospital after alleged driver assault
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans linebacker Jaylen Harrell is in hospital after a car crash in Florida, with police investigating whether he assaulted a taxi driver.
body: The 24-year-old was a back-seat passenger in his hometown of Tampa on Friday morning "when he reportedly assaulted the driver while the vehicle was in motion", Tampa Police said.
According to police, the driver, a man in his mid-30s, swerved and hit another vehicle before crashing into a utility pole.
The rideshare driver sustained minor injuries and was treated at the scene, while the driver of the second vehicle was uninjured.
Tennessee Titans said in a statement, external they are in "constant communication" with Harrell's family and are working to gather further information.

articles.title: 'Completely unacceptable! - Vasseur rebukes Leclerc for Hamilton collision
articles.summary: Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur blamed Charles Leclerc for the "completely unacceptable" collision with team-mate Lewis Hamilton in the Las Vegas Grand Prix.
body: The Ferrari drivers made contact when battling over sixth place with 12 laps remaining in a breathless, frenzied race in which the team were attempting to recover from a poor qualifying when both drivers were knocked out in Q2.
Hamilton was spun around in the Turn Seven-collision, dropping to 10th in the order. Leclerc was found to be at fault by race stewards, who imposed a 10-second penalty on him.
That was applied to Leclerc's final race time and dropped him to 10th place in the final classification, with Hamilton ending up seventh.
Two weeks after speaking to both drivers to remind them of their responsibilities to the team after a squabble on track in Mexico had cost them a likely win, Vasseur was left unimpressed.

articles.title: Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide
articles.summary: Red Bull's Max Verstappen wins an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that featured 34 lead changes and another collision between the Ferraris.
body: Red Bull's Max Verstappen won an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that featured 34 lead changes in a non-stop battle at the front.
The leading group of 10 cars were tied together for the vast majority of the race as the lead constantly changed hands between Verstappen and the Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli.
But Verstappen was the one constant, always seeming a step ahead of his rivals as he debated electrical energy deployment strategy with his team.

And in the final laps Mercedes' challenge unravelled as first Russell made a mistake and crashed trying to pass Antonelli, and the Italian lost out to the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri going into the final lap.

articles.title: 'He's so far below my level' - Verstappen taunts Russell over Las Vegas GP error
articles.summary: Max Verstappen says George Russell is "so far below my level" in a scathing response to the Mercedes driver after winning the Las Vegas Grand Prix.
body: Verstappen claimed his fourth win of the season after a stunning defensive drive while Russell crashed in the latter stages and finished ninth, having battled Verstappen for the win earlier.
The pair collided in final practice on Saturday with Verstappen warned for "driving erratically" in the incident but Russell criticised the Red Bull driver.

"There's nothing in the rules to say you cannot overtake someone who is starting a lap but when you do this, you are screwing this person over and he does this week in, week out with many drivers and everybody accepts it," he told Sky Italy.
"I'm not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they're bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody's got to stand up to that guy."

articles.title: ‘Coward’: Lionel Messi avoiding red card after hitting Gonzalo Tapia in the face angers MLS fans
articles.summary: Lionel Messi faces backlash after hitting Gonzalo Tapia in the face during a throw-in. Inter Miami CF kicked off their defence of the MLS Cup title with a brutal 3-0 defeat in the opening round against Columbus Crew.
body: Miami still have a shot at making a comeback in the best-of-three series, but one moment involving Lionel Messi made headlines in Game 1.
The controversial moment occurred when Miami were trailing 0-1, and Columbus’ Gonzalo Tapia stood too close to the sidelines.
It prevented Messi from having a clear view to take the throw-in, and the 39-year-old was furious. So much so that he threw the ball in Tapia’s face.
Upon seeing the viral clip, a plethora of soccer fans called out the MLS officials not showing a red card to the Inter Miami captain.

articles.title: Pontypool front row inducted into hall of fame
articles.summary: Individually they were wonderfully talented but together, they were fearsome. The Pontypool front row of Tony 'Charlie' Faulkner, Bobby Windsor and Graham Price would become the stuff of rugby legend.
body: The trio were the bulwark of a ferocious club side, the all-conquering Wales team of the Seventies and the British and Irish Lions.
Now, 43 years after Price retired, the last of the trio to do so, they have become the 187th, 188th and 189th inductees of World Rugby's Hall of Fame.
"Rugby is often referred to as the ultimate team sport," said John Eales, chairman of the Hall of Fame panel.
"And yet, within every team there are often units that, through their dominance, style and standards, transcend generations.

articles.title: Verstappen wins wild Las Vegas GP as Ferraris collide again
articles.summary: Max Verstappen produced a remarkable drive to win a wild Las Vegas Grand Prix that saw him withstand extreme pressure from George Russell and Kimi Antonelli before a late Mercedes collapse.
body: Pole-sitter Verstappen retained the lead at the start but the enormous power of a slipstream on the long straights of the Las Vegas Strip Circuit made it impossible for the Dutchman to pull clear, and resulted in 34 changes of the lead and well over 300 total overtakes in the 50-lap race.

First Russell, and then later newly crowned world champion Antonelli were each able to pass Verstappen on multiple occasions but the Red Bull driver calmly retook the lead within a few corners every time, expertly managing the deployment of his power.

Russell, trying to pass his team-mate for second with three laps remaining, ran into a barrier after overshooting a corner and dropped down the order, before Antonelli made an error with his deployment at the start of the final lap that allowed Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri to snatch a double podium for McLaren.
"That was crazy. Really, really surreal and something I've never seen before in F1 myself," Verstappen said.

articles.title: Kim Kardashian supports Lewis Hamilton at Las Vegas Grand Prix
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton has been in the spotlight for nearly two decades as one of the biggest stars in Formula 1. But at this weekend’s Las Vegas Grand Prix, his girlfriend drew plenty of attention of her own.
body: Kim Kardashian was on hand in Las Vegas to support Hamilton, spending Friday night’s qualifying session in the Ferrari garage. She then returned to the paddock on Saturday, arriving for race day in an all-black leather look.

Hamilton and Kardashian were first linked back in February, and they have since become one of the most talked-about couples in sports and entertainment. Kardashian has made several appearances at Grand Prix weekends this year, including in Singapore.
Kardashian has been more guarded about the relationship. In an interview with The Times earlier this fall, she said she was “really single for five years” after her split from ex-husband Kanye West.
“That felt great. I could focus on my kids and projects that I really wanted to be involved with. I really felt no rush,” Kardashian told The Times.

articles.title: Man United Starting XI vs Liverpool: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup
articles.summary: Manchester United Predicted XI vs Liverpool as Mauricio Pochettino Starts at Anfield. Mauricio Pochettino does not get an easing-in period. His first match as Manchester United manager comes at Anfield, against Liverpool, with a handful of training sessions behind him and very little time to impose…
body: That matters, up to a point. Systems do not change overnight and, in this case, there may not be much need for upheaval anyway. Michael Carrick and Pochettino both favour a 4-2-3-1, so the shape should look familiar even if the messaging and intensity inside it are different.

United are still dealing with absences. Carlos Baleba remains out after the hamstring injury he suffered against Roma in the Champions League, while Benjamin Sesko is not expected back until the New Year. Manuel Ugarte is also unavailable, which narrows the midfield options and makes some selections fairly obvious.

The likely side looks straightforward. Lammens should start in goal. Diogo Dalot is expected at right-back, with Luke Shaw having a decent chance of returning on the left if he is fit enough. Lisandro Martinez is back from suspension and should come straight into central defence alongside Harry Maguire.
